claim_being_audited: Whether the model can be certified for launch on the current packet if the certification expressly discloses that documentation-sufficiency evaluation for the named accessibility deployment context is still unevaluated.
decision_criteria: Policy requires material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and passing support/latency/rollback checks support operational launch readiness but do not close named-context evaluation gaps.
Unknown coverage cannot be restated as a passed condition merely because no completed test has failed.
evidence_requests: The final certification or model-card text showing the accessibility-context evaluation gap is explicitly disclosed.
Any approved risk-acceptance record, if the organization intends to certify without that disclosure.
Completed documentation-sufficiency evaluation results for the named accessibility deployment context, if available after the current packet.
specific_concerns: The packet supports launch readiness, but it also shows a named-context evaluation gap that cannot be treated as passed.
The draft model-card statement that there are no known disability accommodations intake limitations is not supported by completed testing; QA says the correct status is unknown.
The action is only compliant if certification is not represented as clean or gap-free and the named accessibility-context gap is explicitly disclosed.
No evidence of approved risk acceptance is present, so disclosure is the only supported path under the policy text provided.
unsupported_claims: Any implication that the named accessibility deployment context has passed documentation-sufficiency evaluation.
Any clean-certification reading of the recommendation without explicit disclosure of the gap.
